drafted_from: tool:serve-a-sites-pages-from-its-rows's own row (its words and settings) and the do-work programs it runs (serve.ts, pages.ts, render.ts)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Serve my site from its page rows on my always-on computer." The AI writes the site's settings file (listen "unix:/run/site/site.sock", origin "https://example.com", the pages database a_site_for_who_uses_it), adds the unit to the computer row with tool:start-a-computer, and then GET https://example.com/sitemap.xml lists every public page.

lists.label: Site pages
lists.holds: One page of the site per row: its address pattern, title, who may open it, its layout tree and the tool whose screen is its main part.
alike: Webflow pages and CMS template pages
a sitemap spreadsheet with one row per page

lists.label: Site look
lists.holds: One CSS variable of the site's look per row: a colour, a font family or a size, written on every page.
alike: design tokens in a theme file

instructions: 1. Make the two tables in the site's own database (pages and site_look, with the fields above) and pour the example rows into them, or into lists you already keep (see pour).

2. Write the site's settings file: listen, origin, lang, door (the engine door and the name of the site's pass credential), pages (the database and the declared use its reads run under), sign_in and, for member files, member_files.
3. Put the unit on the site's computer row and run tool:start-a-computer; the front web server passes the site's name to settings.listen.
4. Open https://<the site>/sitemap.xml and each page address; a members page sends a visitor to sign_in.page and opens for a member of the members team.

worked_examples.title: An article page drawn from its row and its tool's screen
worked_examples.ask: Show the article at /articles/first-serve on my site.
worked_examples.given: The page row {"path": "/articles/:slug", "tool": "tool:read-a-published-article", "input": {"slug": ":slug"}} and the request GET /articles/first-serve
worked_examples.hands_back: The site program runs tool:read-a-published-article with {"slug": "first-serve"} through the door as the site's caller, draws its screen show/Article.tsx with that answer, and answers 200 with the page, Server-Timing naming the run's milliseconds; the same answer opens the same screen in the person's AI app.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for your site's pages (a Webflow pages export, a sitemap sheet) and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than least_coverage of the kit's fields match, and otherwise answers the write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
